author: sjm41
body:
* **InterPro ID / label**
IPR006179 5'-Nucleotidase/apyrase (Family)
IPR008334 5'-Nucleotidase, C-terminal (Domain)
IPR036907 5'-Nucleotidase, C-terminal domain superfamily (Homologous superfamily

* **Example sequences with problematic annotation (ID + gene/protein name):**
Dmel CG30103 (A1ZAU0)

* **Description of issue**
All three of these entries are annotated with the high-level (relatively uninformative) term 'hydrolase activity'.
However Dmel CG30103 (A1ZAU0), at least, has all these signatures but is characterized to be catalytically inactive.

Also, IPR006179 has child terms with more specific/useful GO terms. 
For IPR008334 and IPR036907, I believe the catalytic domain is in the N-terminus, not the C-terminus.

So, maybe remove hydrolase activity from these 3 entries?
title: InterPro2GO issue: IPR006179/IPR008334/IPR036907

author: sarach06
body:
Hi Steven,
Thank you very much. Yes, I agree, the catalytic domain is the N-terminal. I removed the term from the three entries as, as you said it is not very informative and there are some sequences that are inactive. These changes will be available in InterPro 111.0.

Best wishes,
Sara
